key_insight: Pristine graphene flakes (GF) are chemically distinct from graphene oxide flakes (GOF): GF acts as a less disruptive scaffold that organizes perovskite precursors and improves crystallization, while GOF binds more strongly but perturbs the lattice and introduces gap states.
engineering_relevance: Using GF as an additive can boost perovskite solar-cell efficiency and stability, especially in compositions with difficult crystallization, making flake chemistry a practical design lever for device optimization.
method: DFT compared GF vs GOF interactions with perovskite lattices.
Machine-learning atomistic simulations tracked graphene contacts with solvated Pb/I precursor regions.
Spectroscopy linked GF additives to preorganized precursor structures and crystallization behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a champion efficiency increase in mixed Sn-Pb devices from 21.5% to 23.7% with improved storage stability, alongside consistent benefits across perovskite compositions.
watch_item: GF performance depends on solvent and precursor environment, so additive processing conditions may need careful control to reproduce the crystallization and device gains.
paper_title: Understanding Graphene-Perovskite Interactions: From Flake Chemistry to Crystallisation and Solar Cell Performance
